N° 05Security checker for apps built with AI2026

How to use CYVAREN

For people who build web apps with AI coding tools and want a check before launch, freelancers who deliver apps to clients, and developers who want a plain-language report they can share.

Open CYVAREN ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to cyvaren.vercel.app.

2

Click Open the live demo. A read-only workspace opens with three projects already scanned, with no sign-up.

3

Open Sample: vulnerable Express API, then Security, and click a failed check to see its findings.

4

Click a finding to read the evidence, the fix and how to check it worked.

5

Create a free account to scan your own app: upload a .zip of the project or paste a public GitHub address.

6

To use AI, a workspace owner turns on AI assistance in Settings. The demo account cannot use AI.

02

Features

01

Dashboard

The latest scan of the selected project at a glance: the six checks with their status, open findings by severity, and every action. Actions that exist are links; planned ones are marked with their milestone, never shown as working.

STEPS

  1. Pick a project in the selector at the top
  2. Read the status of each check
  3. Click Open findings
02

Six security checks

Six checks with plain names: Only your own stuff, Real authentication, Keys out of your code, Lock admin pages, Limit password tries and Update old parts. Each says passed, failed, not tested or inconclusive, what it examined and what it could not see.

STEPS

  1. Open a project, then Security
  2. Click a check to filter its findings
  3. Read Coverage and limitations at the bottom
03

A finding, explained

Each finding shows the code that triggered it, whether it is confirmed or only suspected, an explanation in plain words and a technical one, the impact, the fix and how to verify it. Copy fix for my AI tool puts all of it on the clipboard as a prompt.

STEPS

  1. Click a finding in the list
  2. Switch between In plain words and Technical
  3. Click Copy fix for my AI tool
  4. Under Triage, mark it fixed, accepted risk or false positive
04

Architecture map

Every page, API route, database and outside service, and how they connect, drawn from the code. Each link points to the code that proves it, a security overlay marks the paths to data that need no login, and Problems lists circular dependencies and tangled modules.

STEPS

  1. Open Architecture
  2. Search a component, file or route
  3. Keep Security overlay on
  4. Open the Problems tab
05

Explain my application

A written tour of the app in six versions: beginner, developer, architect, security, product owner and executive. Every sentence is built from facts found in the code, with references, and no AI is used on this page.

STEPS

  1. Open Explain
  2. Pick an audience
  3. Open Evidence under a section
  4. Trace one endpoint from request to database
06

Ask AI about a finding

With AI assistance on, Explain for my code sends the finding and the lines around it to Claude and returns what is wrong, why it matters and a fix written for your code. Secret values are replaced with placeholders before anything is sent.

STEPS

  1. Open a finding
  2. Under Ask AI, click Explain for my code
  3. Check the answer against your code
07

Repair Studio

Draft a fix asks Claude for a change to one file. CYVAREN then re-scans a copy of the code with the change applied and says whether the finding is gone and whether anything new appeared. For a vulnerable library, Draft the upgrade edits package.json without AI, choosing the smallest safe version, and checks it on OSV.dev. You get the diff, a .patch file and the command to apply it; nothing in your project is changed.

STEPS

  1. On a finding, click Draft a fix
  2. Read the re-scan result
  3. Download the .patch or copy the diff
  4. Apply it yourself, then scan again
08

Project assistant

Ask about a project in plain words: what to fix first, which routes have no login check. Answers come from the latest scan, the source files are not sent, and the conversation is not stored.

STEPS

  1. Open Assistant
  2. Pick a starter question or type your own
  3. Ask a follow-up
09

Reports and fix verification

Export each scan as Markdown for people, SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning, or JSON. Verify fixes compares two scans and lists what was resolved, what is new and what is still open.

STEPS

  1. Open Reports
  2. Choose a scan
  3. Download a format
  4. After a re-scan, click Verify fixes on Security
10

AI on your terms

AI is off for every workspace until an owner or admin turns it on. Settings shows the provider, the model, how many of the day's requests were used and exactly what is sent for each feature, and each switch is written to the audit log.

STEPS

  1. Open Settings
  2. Under AI assistance, turn it on or off
  3. Read What is sent, and when
03Tips
  • Start with the demo: the vulnerable sample shows every kind of finding, and the hardened sample shows what passing looks like.
  • Suspected means a pattern in the code matched and needs a human look; confirmed means the evidence is certain, such as a key in a file.
  • A passed check is not a guarantee: read what each check could not test, listed under it.
04FAQ
Does CYVAREN run my code?

No. It reads the files and analyses them as text. Nothing in the project is installed or executed, and uploaded archives are unpacked with protection against path tricks, links and archives built to exhaust memory.

Is my code sent to an AI?

Only if your workspace turns AI assistance on, and only when someone presses an AI button. Then the finding with nearby code, or the one file being fixed, goes to Anthropic with secret values replaced by placeholders. The six checks never use AI.

Which apps does it understand?

JavaScript and TypeScript. Route checks work for Next.js API routes, Express, Fastify, Koa and Hono. Front-end-only apps still get the secret, dependency and build-pipeline checks.

Can it fix my app for me?

It drafts the fix and re-scans it, and you review and apply it. Opening pull requests and running your tests in a sandbox are planned.

Is it free?

Yes, during early access: up to five apps per workspace and a daily number of AI requests. Paid plans are planned and shown as such.
